ans: Race a can down a ramp against a block sliding with no friction, and the can loses. Some of the pull goes into spinning it up instead. a_CM = ((m*g*sin(theta))/(m+(I_CM/r^2))), and I_CM is the tax.

q: How do you find the rotational power?
record: P=tau*omega | P:W tau:N*m omega:1/s | missing:tau | standard conditions | fit:high
ans: P = tau*omega is how you get shaft torque out of an engine rating. You know the watts, you know the revs, the twist falls out. Gearing only trades them: at the wheels, big tau comes with small omega.

q: What does kirchhoff junction rule say?
record: I_1=I_2+I_3 | I_1:A I_2:A I_3:A | missing:I_2 | standard conditions | fit:high
ans: Each junction hands you one equation, which is what makes the rule worth having: I_1 = I_2 + I_3. Collect enough of them and you can solve for currents you cannot reach with a meter.

q: how is the centripetal acceleration related to the other quantities?
record: a=(v)^(2)/r | a:m/s^2 v:m/s r:m | missing:v | standard conditions | fit:high
ans: Round a curve at steady speed and you are still accelerating, because your direction keeps changing. a = v^2/r points straight at the center. Centripetal is Latin for center seeking.

q: given h = 6.626e-34, what is binding energy of an electron?
record: E_b=h*f_O | E_b:J h:J*s f_O:Hz | missing:f_O | standard conditions | fit:high
ans: Shine dim blue light on sodium and electrons jump off. Shine bright red light and nothing comes out at all. There is a threshold frequency f_O, and E_b = h*f_O is how tightly that electron was held.

q: What does motionally induced emf depend on?
record: epsilon=B*l*v | epsilon:V B:T l:m v:m/s | missing:B | standard conditions | fit:high
ans: The v is the catch. A wire sitting still in a magnetic field makes nothing, and one drifting along the field makes nothing either. It has to cut across. Then epsilon = B*l*v and your bike light glows.

q: What does centripetal acceleration depend on?
record: a=(v)^(2)/r | a:m/s^2 v:m/s r:m | missing:v | standard conditions | fit:high
ans: Nothing pulls you outward in a turn. a = v^2/r is the acceleration aimed inward that keeps you on the circle, and what you feel is the seat shoving you toward the center to supply it.

q: Define total entropy change of system and surroundings.
record: Delta_S_tot=Delta_S_h+Delta_S_c | Delta_S_tot:J/K Delta_S_h:J/K Delta_S_c:J/K | missing:Delta_S_h | standard conditions | fit:high
ans: Delta_S_tot = Delta_S_h + Delta_S_c watches both ends of a heat flow at once. Only a reversible step holds it at zero; a real temperature gap always pushes it up. Heat will not run back uphill.
